title: General two-stage restriction bound
statement:
Let $p_1, p_2 \in (0,1]$, let $E$ and $A$ be events on restrictions of $n$ variables, and let $\beta \ge 0$. Write $\Pr_p[\,\cdot\,]$ for the probability of an event under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction, and for restrictions $\rho_1, \rho_2$ let $\rho_1 \circ \rho_2$ denote their composition (the values fixed by $\rho_1$, filled in by $\rho_2$ on the coordinates $\rho_1$ leaves free). Suppose that for every restriction $\rho_1$ for which $A(\rho_1)$ fails, one has $\Pr_{p_2}[\,E(\rho_1 \circ \rho_2)\,] \le \beta$. Then
\[
  \Pr_{p_1 p_2}[E] \;\le\; \Pr_{p_1}[A] + \beta .
\]
hypotheses_covered: for every ρ₁ with ¬A(ρ₁), the Bernoulli(p₂)-probability of E(ρ₁ ∘ ρ₂) is at most β
replaced:
Let $0 < p_1,p_2 \le 1$, let $E$ be an event on restrictions and $A$ a ``failure''
event, and let $\beta \ge 0$. If for every $\rho_1$ with $\lnot A(\rho_1)$ the
conditional probability $\Pr_{p_2}[E(\mathrm{composeRestr}\,\rho_1\,\rho_2)] \le \beta$, then
$\Pr_{p_1 p_2}[E] \le \Pr_{p_1}[A] + \beta$.
